messages:
sam-sales: Galileo wants a short presales note: PCI/PHI inference must hit their on-prem DLP; everything else can use Redwood hosted. Need connectivity patterns, minimal firewall snippet, who pays for PrivateLink, and src-ip preservation options by EOD.

nina-solutions: Pattern options: 1) VPC peering/TGW -> route sensitive subnets to customer's egress (can preserve src-ip with passthrough NLB). 2) PrivateLink interface endpoint -> simpler surface but usually SNATs source IP. 3) Tag-based routing: send sensitive models to a private deployment that egresses to customer.

rob-netops: Netops constraints from customer: no 0.0.0.0/0 egress, SNI visible for TLS-inspect, retention of client identifiers in logs. If src-ip is required, they must provision an NLB with proxy-protocol v2 in front of the connector.

tara-security: For POC we recommend TLS passthrough. MITM/TLS-inspect requires customer-supplied certs and a data-handling plan and will need security review.

mike-ops: Quick allowlist snippet (replace sample CIDRs):
- Destination: 52.20.0.0/16  # sample redwood edge
- Ports: TCP 443
- SNI: allow *.redwood.ai
- DNS: restrict to customer resolver or use endpoint-aware DNS

infra-bot: note: AWS interface endpoint charges are on the customer. Redwood may recommend temporary Dedicated burst capacity if proxied traffic is high (billable).

nina-solutions: POC checklist:
- Customer: provide exact CIDRs and SNI hostnames
- Customer: decide on src-ip preservation; if yes provision NLB + enable proxy-protocol
- Customer: indicate TLS passthrough vs MITM; if MITM provide cert chain and data-handling doc
- Redwood: provision staging PrivateLink connector or peering and enable model-route tagging for sensitive workloads
- Redwood: run 15-min perf test with synthetic sensitive payloads and verify client ids in logs

sam-sales: Assignments: @nina-solutions draft Dedicated estimate, @rob-netops final allowlist CIDRs, @tara-security CISO paragraph. I'll send to Galileo tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
